newsitem.title: USA: OUTLOOK-U.S. cheese price recovery seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: OUTLOOK-U.S. cheese price recovery seen continuing.

text.p: Wholesale cheese prices in the U.S. should recover this year from the crash in late 1996 but farm milk prices should be below year-ago levels, said U.S. Department of Agriculture economist James Miller.

"Butter and cheese prices have both recovered somewhat from December lows. Additional recovery in cheese prices is expected and may also be in store for butter prices," he said in papers issued at USDA's annual agricultural outlook forum.
He noted a sharp slide in prices late last year "proved to be an over-reaction" to falling sales and signs that stocks were not declining normally.

Miller forecast that farm milk prices in 1997 would run below a year earlier throughout this year. He noted, however, that projected 1997 prices would be relatively high compared with the late eighties and early nineties.

He said the average rise in retail dairy prices of one to three percent was anticipated with a large increase in the premium of retail to farm prices expected, particularly during the first half of the year.
In the export sector Miller forecast that the expansion in world export supplies would keep pace with world import demand. World prices were seen generally below U.S. prices.
"The restrictions on EU (European Union) cheese subsidies and growing import demand are expected to make cheese markets the strongest of the international dairy markets," he said.

"Pizza alone is creating markets for cheese which never existed before," he added, noting an aggressive expansion of cheese capacity in New Zealand and Australia promised to keep prices from deviating too far from parity with milk and nonfat dry milk.
